c.tagline: Australia's beach-holiday capital of surf, high-rises, theme parks, and green hinterland.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered (GC Cabs is the main operator); a booking fee applies for phone or app bookings and airport pickups add a surcharge.

emergency.note: 000 is the primary emergency number; 112 also works from any mobile and 106 is the text-based line for the deaf or speech-impaired.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Main Beach: Tedder Avenue Main Beach Gold Coast

avoid.reason: The Surfers Paradise nightlife strip gets rowdy with alcohol-fuelled trouble late at night, especially during Schoolies Week; always swim between the flags on patrolled beaches.

hood_desc: The high-rise heart of the Gold Coast, where a golden surf beach meets Cavill Avenue's shops, bars, and nightclubs; brash, busy, and the classic first-timer base for beach days and late nights.
A more polished beachside district just south of Surfers, home to The Star casino, the Pacific Fair mall, and a strip of acclaimed restaurants and cafes; upscale dining with the tram at the door.
An exclusive enclave between the Broadwater and the ocean, known for chic Tedder Avenue, the marina at Marina Mirage, and Sea World nearby; refined, low-key, and moneyed.
A laid-back, hip surf town wrapped around a headland national park, with a famous point break, buzzing James Street eateries, and a village feel; the coast's coolest, most relaxed pocket.
The southernmost twin-town beach community by the NSW border and the airport, with classic surf beaches at Kirra and Rainbow Bay; nostalgic, uncrowded, and family-friendly.
lodging: The Star Grand at The Star Gold Coast

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout Australia.

transit.hours: The G:link tram runs roughly 5am to midnight (24 hours on peak weekends), with buses on similar hours; Queensland Rail Gold Coast line trains connect the western suburbs to Brisbane.
transit.note: One TransLink network covers the G:link light rail running along the coast from Helensvale through Surfers Paradise and Broadbeach, the Kinetic Surfside bus network, and the Gold Coast heavy-rail line to Brisbane.
transit.pay: Tap on and off with a go card or a contactless Visa, Mastercard, or Amex card or phone; since 2024 every journey across South East Queensland is a flat 50-cent fare, with transfers included.

bus: Coaches to Brisbane, Byron Bay and northern NSW

transit.m: Route 777 express bus to Broadbeach South G:link, then tram (~45 min)
Taxi or rideshare to Surfers Paradise (25-35 min)
